sents.t: Another one of yours: most of the gains in life come from suffering in the short term so you can get paid in the long term.
sents.zh: 你还有一句话：人生中大部分收获，都来自短期的吃苦，这样你才能在长期得到回报。

sents.t: That’s classic. That’s the marshmallow test on a daily basis.
sents.zh: 这很经典，就是每天都在做的棉花糖实验。

sents.t: But there’s an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming a suffering addict,
sents.zh: 但这里有个有意思的问题，我觉得人们要避免变成一个“吃苦上瘾”的人，

sents.t: sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
sents.zh: 就是把吃苦本身当成进步的标志，而不是看吃苦带来的结果。对吧？

sents.t: It’s like, I was in pain not eating the marshmallow. I was in pain doing this work.
sents.zh: 就好像：我忍着没吃棉花糖，好痛苦；我做这份工作，好痛苦。

sents.t: I have attached well-being and satisfaction to pain, not to what the pain gets me on the other side of it.
sents.zh: 我把幸福感和满足感绑在了痛苦上，而不是绑在痛苦最终能带给我的东西上。

sents.t: If you define pain as physical pain, then it’s a real thing, it happens, and you can’t ignore it, but that’s not what we mean by suffering.
sents.zh: 如果把痛苦定义为身体上的疼痛，那它是真实存在的，会发生，你没法无视它，但我们说的“受苦”不是这个意思。

sents.t: Suffering is mostly mental anguish and mental pain, and it just means you don’t wanna do the task at hand.
sents.zh: 受苦主要是精神上的煎熬和痛苦，说白了就是你不想做眼前这件事。

sents.t: If you were fine doing the task at hand then you wouldn’t be suffering,
sents.zh: 如果你乐意做眼前的事，你就不会觉得受苦，

sents.t: and then the question is what’s more effective: to suffer along the way or just to interpret it in a way that it’s not suffering?
sents.zh: 那问题就变成了：哪个更有效——一路受着苦，还是换个角度去理解，让它不再是受苦？

sents.t: You hear from a lot of successful people, they look back and they say, “Oh the journey was the fun part.”
sents.zh: 你会听到很多成功人士回头看时说：“哦，其实过程才是最有趣的部分。”

sents.t: That was actually the entertaining part and I should have enjoyed it more.
sents.zh: 那其实才是最好玩的部分，我当时应该更享受它。
